lines.say: a lab-made tail piece of growth hormone that doesn't bind its receptor (lab tests)
more fat burning and less weight gain in obese mice (mouse study)
missed its weight-loss goal in a 24-week, 502-person trial; earlier gains were small
no change in IGF-1 versus placebo in six human trials, unlike growth hormone
no change in glucose tolerance in human trials; no rise in blood sugar in mice
better knee joint healing (rabbit study); FDA didn't evaluate joint uses
possible immune reactions; injecting it has no human data, and FDA can't rule them out
serious adverse events that may be linked to it, cause unclear, FDA says
possible liver cell changes in toxicity testing (monkey study)

ask: Which approved weight-loss options fit me, given that AOD-9604 failed its main trial?
